vulnerabilities.description: API key hardcoded in source code
vulnerabilities.risk: Exposure of sensitive credentials in version control, accessible to anyone with code access
vulnerabilities.fix: Move API_KEY to environment variables using os.getenv()

vulnerabilities.description: User input directly formatted into SQL query without parameterization
vulnerabilities.vulnerable_code: sql = "SELECT id, username FROM users WHERE username LIKE '%{}%'".format(name)
vulnerabilities.risk: Attacker can execute arbitrary SQL commands, extract data, modify database, or perform authentication bypass
vulnerabilities.secure_replacement:
sql = "SELECT id, username FROM users WHERE username LIKE ?"
cur.execute(sql, ('%' + name + '%',))

vulnerabilities.description: Using pickle.loads() on untrusted user input
vulnerabilities.risk: Remote Code Execution (RCE) - attacker can craft malicious pickle data to execute arbitrary code
vulnerabilities.fix: Use safe deserialization like json.loads() or validate pickle data with strict protocols
vulnerabilities.secure_replacement:
import json
data = request.get_json()
profile = data

vulnerabilities.description: User input directly concatenated into os.system() command
vulnerabilities.risk: Command injection - attacker can execute arbitrary shell commands with application privileges
vulnerabilities.fix: Use subprocess module with shell=False and pass arguments as list

vulnerabilities.description: User input unsanitized in Jinja2 template via string formatting
vulnerabilities.risk: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) - attacker can inject JavaScript or HTML to execute malicious scripts
vulnerabilities.fix: Use Jinja2 variable escaping or avoid render_template_string
vulnerabilities.secure_replacement:
from markupsafe import escape return f"

Hello {escape(name)}

"

vulnerabilities.type: Hardcoded Credentials & Plain Text Password Storage
vulnerabilities.description: User passwords stored in plain text in source code
vulnerabilities.risk: Exposure of user credentials in version control; plain text comparison vulnerable to brute force attacks
vulnerabilities.fix: Use password hashing (bcrypt/argon2) and load user data from secure database with hashed passwords

vulnerabilities.description: Flask debug mode enabled which exposes sensitive information
vulnerabilities.risk: Debug mode reveals stack traces, environment variables, and source code to attackers
vulnerabilities.fix: Disable debug mode in production; use environment variable to control
vulnerabilities.cwe: CWE-215: Information Exposure Through Debug Information

summary.recommendation: All vulnerabilities must be fixed before deploying to production. Implement the secure replacements provided and conduct follow-up security testing.
